# What Happens to a House After the Founder? — complete editable platform copy

## 1. LONG VIDEO
Put four Worth records on a timeline. State only what the records prove, then reveal the missing governance layer. Run the house through stabilize, locate, interpret, account.

## 2. SHORT 01
“A name continuing is evidence of continuity. It is not proof that everything continued.” Split attribution, company, method, people, archive, rights, and obligations.

## 3. SHORT 02
“The first succession decision may be to pause.” Stabilize obligations before announcing a creative heir.

## 4. CAROUSEL
THE FOUNDER IS ABSENT / PEOPLE / ORDERS / MONEY / KEYS / IP / ARCHIVE / AUTHORITY / METHOD / SUCCESSOR / CORRECTION / CONTINUE OR CLOSE.

## 5. NEWSLETTER
Subject: What exactly survives when the founder does not? Use the Worth record sequence to distinguish public continuity from institutional continuity.

## 6. BOARD / ESTATE BRIEF
Six scenarios—continue, pause, license, sell, donate, close—with responsible authority, affected stakeholders, evidence, risks, and counsel gates.

## Claim ledger
- **VERIFIED:** The Met records House of Worth garments made both before and after Charles Frederick Worth’s 1895 death under the continuing design-house attribution. (S68, S69, S71)
- **INFERENCE:** A continuing house name does not prove continuity of authorship, governance, ownership, labor, or method. (S68, S69, S71)
- **PROPOSAL:** Succession planning should separately map company authority, IP, archive custody, employment, obligations, access, and public interpretation. (S63, S64, S65)
